english.title: Falsify, conceal, suppress or destroy data / device in vehicle in breach Art 32(3)
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF THE OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 97(1)(a)(iii) of the Transport Act 1968.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
use or cause or permit to be used
vehicle to which section 97 applies
in breach of Art 32(3) of the EU Tachographs Regulation (EU) No 165/2014
by falsifying or concealing or suppressing or destroy data recorded on the record sheet OR
stored in the tachograph or on the driver card or print-outs from the tachograph OR
device present in vehicle which could be used to this effect

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 97(7) of the Transport Act 1968 defines the EU Tachographs Regulation as Regulation (EU) No 165/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council on tachographs in road transport as read with the Community Drivers' Hours and Recording Equipment Regulations 2007 (SI 2007/1819).

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 monthsNote
Note that for offences committed since 12 March 2015, section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 removes the limits on certain fines given by the Magistrates' Courts. Offences that were previously punishable by fines of 'prescribed sums' and that were limited to 'not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale' or 'not exceeding the statutory maximum', are now punishable by a fine of any amount.
